title: Sandbox relay with callstack checkpoints and injection throttle
creator: Sanjay Mehta
description: Implement a sandboxed relay layer for multi-tool invocations that introduces callstack checkpoints, idempotency tokens, and an injection throttle to prevent unbounded recursion and noisy tool-result injection into streaming responses. This ticket covers design, integration with the streaming API and function-calling surface, a lightweight compatibility shim for legacy SDK clients, and tests for correctness and performance.
acceptance_criteria: Relay accepts a tool invocation sequence and emits a deterministic, ordered stream of tokens and structured tool-result events to clients.
Callstack checkpoints are created at every tool boundary and persisted to short-term memstore; replay for idempotent re-invocations is supported via idempotency tokens.
Injection throttle enforces configurable soft/hard limits: max_injections_per_request (default 4) and max_injection_rate (tokens/sec), and triggers a graceful fallback when exceeded.
Compatibility shim translates legacy function-calling payloads (v1 SDK) to the new structured events without dropping streaming semantics.
Automated tests cover recursion depth > 10, circular tool dependency detection, streaming latency regression (< 10% overhead), and structured output schema conformance.
Design review approved by runtime and SDK leads; PR merged to main and feature-flagged rollout plan documented.
design_decisions: Use a lightweight sandbox relay process per request group that mediates between core executor and tool adapters to avoid tool-level side-effects in the main runtime.
Callstack checkpoints will store (call_id, parent_id, depth, last_token_index, idempotency_token) in an in-memory memstore with optional persistence to Redis for Dedicated/Private deployments.
Idempotency tokens are issued by relay on first tool call; subsequent identical calls matched by signature+token will return cached tool results to prevent duplicate side-effects.

Injection throttle separated into two controls: soft throttle (signals warning event in stream, allows best-effort partial injection) and hard throttle (truncates injection and emits structured error event), configurable per-customer via policy.
Streaming integration: structured tool-result events are emitted inline as JSONL events over the existing SSE/streaming channel to preserve order while allowing incremental parsing by clients.
Compatibility shim maps legacy SDK function-call responses into the structured event format and exposes a feature flag to enable deprecation telemetry.
Circular-dependency detection uses a Bloom filter of callstack hashes to keep memory small while still catching typical cycles; false positives are handled conservatively by emitting a backoff event.
Security: sandbox relay will run with restricted privileges; tool adapters must explicitly declare side-effect capability and be subject to runtime allowlist.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (spike): prototype relay process and streaming structured events using SSE; wire up idempotency token issuance.
Phase 2: implement callstack checkpoint memstore and replay API; add Bloom-filter cycle detector and injection throttle enforcement.
Phase 3: compatibility shim for v1 SDK (translate incoming function-call shapes, emit legacy-compatible events) and add telemetry for deprecation.
Telemetry: emit metrics for injection_count, throttle_tripped_count, avg_stream_latency_ms, cache_hit_rate_for_idempotent_calls.
Config: expose max_injections_per_request and max_injection_rate as runtime-configurable flags with customer-level overrides in Dedicated/Private.
Testing: unit tests for checkpoint correctness, integration tests with streaming client harness, chaos test that simulates noisy tool generating a flood of small injections.
Docs: update API reference with examples for streaming tool-result events and migration notes for v1 SDK users.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with runtime, SDK, and security. Agreed on event format for inline tool-result JSONL and idempotency token semantics.

2026-02-17: Spike complete. Prototype emits structured events via SSE with acceptable latency (avg +6% CPU). Observed a memory pattern for deep callstacks; decided to cap checkpoint retention to 30s by default.
2026-02-23: Implemented Bloom-filter cycle detection and basic throttle counters. Discovered false-positive trade-offs; tuned parameters to minimize production noise.
2026-03-01: Compatibility shim MVP ready. SDK lead reviewed mapping and requested preserving legacy 'tool_name' field; we added that alias in structured events.
2026-03-03: Security reviewed sandbox design; requested explicit allowlist for adapters and an audit log entry for each idempotent-cache hit. Addressing in next PR.
2026-03-03: Current status: relay prototype feature-flagged in staging, basic end-to-end tests passing. Next: hard-throttle behavior and performance regression tests.
